title: A phenotypic paradigm for cerebral palsy genetics.

verified.what_i_actually_checked: Europe PMC record (PMID 42692005): not open access, no PMC copy, no supplement, no text-mined accessions, no NCBI links to GEO/SRA/dbGaP. Zenodo search for the cohort returned nothing relevant.
verified.what_came_from_paper_text_only: Everything else, from the abstract only: 515 literature-curated genes, 89 with significant CP (cerebral palsy) association, a 460-child genome-sequencing cohort from Shriners Children's, P/LP (pathogenic or likely pathogenic) variants in 15.8% of children across 60 genes.

a1_downloadable.note: No downloadable data found; paper paywalled with no PMC copy. Pediatric genome sequences would be controlled access or unshared (repository not stated in the abstract). Checked Europe PMC and Zenodo only.

a2_label_is_a_column.note: No table seen. The plausible label (gene-level CP association yes/no) would be a statistical test output from the authors' literature curation, not a measured column.

a5_enough_rows.note: Per abstract: 515 genes (89 positive) or 460 children (~73 with a P/LP finding). Both far too small for a useful model; no rows verified.

a6_fits_laptop.note: A gene table would be tiny; raw genomes would be off-limits anyway.

a8_label_provenance.note: The gene association label comes from the authors' statistical test on literature-curated case counts, so it is derived rather than measured.

honest_claim_h3: No model is possible: there are no accessible data, and the abstract's counts (89 positive genes, 460 children) are too small.

plain_idea.one_liner: Use gene features to predict which disease genes raise cerebral palsy risk.
plain_idea.train_on: One row per gene among 515 literature-curated genes. Count taken from the abstract, not verified.
plain_idea.predict: Whether a gene has significant evidence of cerebral palsy association, as decided by the authors' statistical test on published case reports.
plain_idea.why_worthwhile: Clinical geneticists could use it to prioritise which variants found in children with cerebral palsy are likely causal.

ml_idea: Gene-level classifier of cerebral palsy association. Not feasible: no accessible data, and only 89 positives.

effort.cheapest_killing_check: Find out whether the 515-gene curation table is public (for example in the Robinson lab's phenopacket-store on GitHub). Even if it is, 89 positives is too few.

verdict_reason: Paywalled paper with no accessible data files. The sequencing cohort is 460 children, likely controlled access, and the gene-level label is a derived test result with only 89 positives out of 515.
